chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: Arriving in New York in 1912 and living with his sister
summary: He came to New York in 1912 aged eleven, lived with his older sister at 24 West 134th Street and went to school; a grandson of hers worked in radio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay, so you came up to New York in what year?
And your parents had what, both died near the same --
More or less. Yes, an average of about two years difference.
And I came up to New York.
And you lived with your older sister then?
My older sister, she is still alive.
Yes, she's in a nursing home in -- what is it, the Bronx -- what's the name of it Capital Parkway, what's the name of it?
She's in a nursing -- she sold her home when I went back in '74, to one of her grandsons.
Yes, the boy I told you about in one of my letters who is also a jazz historian.
I think he is still with Arlene Francis' show, at WOR.
That we all are. Yes. That's where he was when I was there. He made a what you call, a show. We had Doc Cheatham to be on the show.
So then when you came to New York in 1912, and you were then, what, nine years old, I guess.
And then you began -- were you going to school there, in New York?
Yes, I went to school, yes. There on 135th Street.
What's that, Seventh Avenue? Is that Lenox Avenue?
Lenox Avenue, yes, between Lenox and Fifth.
Right. Right up there where the Schomburg thing is --
Right. Not far from the Lenox Casino, the old Lenox Casino.
